transcript.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to EnglishPod.
So, Marco, how are you doing today?
I'm really happy to be back, ready to deliver another great podcast for all our listeners.
transcript.zh: 我很高兴回来，准备为所有听众带来又一期精彩的播客。

transcript.en: And we've got an intermediate lesson today about spending money.
transcript.zh: 今天我们有一节关于花钱的中级课程。

transcript.en: Yeah, specifically spending money in a company.
transcript.zh: 是的，具体来说是公司里的花钱问题。

transcript.en: We're going to be listening to a business meeting as a company describes how they're spending money.
transcript.zh: 我们要听一个商务会议，一家公司在讨论他们是怎么花钱的。

transcript.en: And they're actually looking at their profit and loss statement.
transcript.zh: 他们实际上在看他们的损益表。

transcript.en: Well, Marco, can you tell us a little bit about a profit and loss statement?
transcript.zh: 马可，你能给我们讲讲损益表是什么吗？

transcript.en: Well, all companies come out with a profit and loss statement every year or every three months.
transcript.zh: 所有公司每年或每季度都会出具一份损益表。

transcript.en: And it's basically a document that shows all the money that the company is spending and all the money that the company is earning.
transcript.zh: 它基本上就是一份文件，显示公司所有的支出和所有的收入。

transcript.en: So it's a document that outlines how much money the company makes and how much it spends.
transcript.zh: 所以它是一份概述公司赚了多少钱和花了多少钱的文件。

transcript.en: So in the end, basically, it'll tell you we're making money or we're losing money.
transcript.zh: 所以最后，它基本上会告诉你：我们在赚钱还是在亏钱。

transcript.en: So we're going to be listening to some people discuss a profit and loss statement in just a moment.
transcript.zh: 我们稍后就要听几个人讨论损益表了。

transcript.en: But before we do that, it's time for vocabulary preview.
transcript.zh: 但在此之前，是词汇预览时间。

transcript.en: So today on our vocabulary preview, we have two words for you.
transcript.zh: 今天的词汇预览，我们为大家准备两个词。

transcript.en: So let's take a look at the first one.
So expenses are things that you have to spend money on regularly.
transcript.zh: Expenses 是你必须定期花钱的东西。

transcript.en: So for example, in a company, regular company expenses are salaries or office supplies or the phone bills, internet bills.
transcript.zh: 比如，在一家公司里，常规的公司开支包括工资、办公用品、电话费、网费。

transcript.en: Maybe in a household or a family, your expenses might be your food, perhaps your transportation or your rent or your heating bill.
transcript.zh: 在一个家庭里，你的开支可能包括食物、交通、房租或暖气费。

transcript.en: So these are all things you spend money on regularly.
transcript.zh: 所以这些都是你定期花钱的东西。

transcript.en: Let's take a look at our second word.
So when something is through the roof, it's...
transcript.zh: 当某物 through the roof 的时候，意思是……

transcript.en: So for example, we can talk about gas prices are through the roof lately.
transcript.zh: 比如，我们可以说最近油价飞涨。

transcript.en: Gas prices have gone really high in the past couple of months.
transcript.zh: 过去几个月油价确实涨得很高。

transcript.en: So when we talk about through the roof, it means that the number is really high.
transcript.zh: 所以当我们说 through the roof，意思是数字非常高。

transcript.en: We typically use this word with numbers.
transcript.zh: 我们通常把这个词和数字一起使用。

transcript.en: It also gives you the idea that the number has risen really quickly.
transcript.zh: 它还给人一种数字上升得非常快的感觉。
所以 through the roof——飞涨。

transcript.en: All right, Marco, do you think it's time for the dialogue?
transcript.zh: 好了，马可，你觉得该听对话了吗？

transcript.en: Yep, let's listen to the dialogue.
As always, the first dialogue is going to be a little bit fast, so it might be a little bit difficult, but...
transcript.zh: 和往常一样，第一遍对话会有点快，所以可能有点难，但是……

transcript.en: Don't worry if you don't understand everything, because we will explain all of the key language in a minute.
transcript.zh: 如果你没完全听懂也不用担心，因为我们马上会解释所有关键的语言点。

transcript.en: Okay, so now the last point on our agenda.
transcript.zh: 好的，现在是我们议程的最后一点。

transcript.en: Jill, let's go over the profit and loss statement.
transcript.zh: 吉尔，我们来过一遍损益表。

transcript.en: Well, the main issue here, as you can see, is that our expenses are through the roof.
transcript.zh: 嗯，如你所见，主要问题是我们的开支飞涨。

transcript.en: These numbers are off the charts.
Well, sir, the company expenditures on entertainment and travel are out of control.
transcript.zh: 嗯，先生，公司在娱乐和差旅方面的支出失控了。

transcript.en: Look at these bills, for example.
Just this month, we've paid over $20,000 for hotel charges.
transcript.zh: 仅这个月，我们就支付了超过两万美元的酒店费用。

transcript.en: The list goes on and on.
Here, this is a bill for $5,000 for spa treatment.
transcript.zh: 这里，这是一张五千美元的水疗账单。

transcript.en: $5,000 were expensed in one night at a place called Wild Things?
transcript.zh: 在一个叫 Wild Things 的地方一晚就花了五千美元？

transcript.en: Thank you for your very thorough analysis.
transcript.zh: 感谢你非常详尽的分析。

transcript.en: Okay, so this accountant, she's pretty thorough, hey?
transcript.zh: 好的，这位会计，她可真够仔细的，对吧？

transcript.en: She's really persistent about her job, and the manager apparently is a little bit embarrassed.
transcript.zh: 她对工作非常执着，而那位经理显然有点尴尬。

transcript.en: I wonder why that could be.
transcript.zh: 我想知道为什么会这样。

transcript.en: Well, we'll talk about that in a little while.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我们稍后会讨论这个。

transcript.en: Why don't we take a look at our language takeaway for today?
transcript.zh: 我们来看看今天的语言要点吧？

transcript.en: In today's language takeaway, we're going to look at three words, and the first word is expenditures.
transcript.zh: 今天的语言要点中，我们要看三个词，第一个词是 expenditures（支出/开支）。

transcript.en: So expenditures sounds pretty close to expenses, right?
transcript.zh: Expenditures 听起来和 expenses 很接近，对吧？

transcript.en: It's pretty similar, but it has a little bit of a difference.
transcript.zh: 非常相似，但有一点区别。

transcript.en: So why don't we listen to some examples and see if we can understand?
transcript.zh: 我们来听几个例子，看看能不能理解。

transcript.en: If elected president, I will increase expenditures on health and education by 12%.
transcript.zh: 如果当选总统，我将把卫生和教育支出增加12%。

transcript.en: We really need to control our travel expenditures.
transcript.zh: 我们真的需要控制差旅支出。

transcript.en: From now on, all managers will fly economy class.
transcript.zh: 从现在起，所有经理都要坐经济舱。

transcript.en: Because of the rise in oil prices, expenditures on food are higher than they have ever been.
transcript.zh: 由于油价上涨，食品支出比以往任何时候都高。

transcript.en: So expenditures is the total amount of money that you're spending on something.
transcript.zh: 所以 expenditures 是你花在某件事上的总金额。

transcript.en: That's the total amount of money versus expenses is the things that you spend money on.
transcript.zh: 那是总金额，而 expenses 是你花钱的具体项目。

transcript.en: Our next word is out of control.
transcript.zh: 下一个词是 out of control（失控）。

transcript.en: So when something is out of control, it's crazy.
transcript.zh: 当某物 out of control，就是疯了、失控了。

transcript.en: Now, let's take a look at our last word for today.
transcript.zh: 现在看今天的最后一个词。

transcript.en: So go over is a pretty simple word.
transcript.zh: Go over 是一个相当简单的词。

transcript.en: Why don't we listen to some examples so we can understand go over?
transcript.zh: 我们来听几个例子来理解 go over 吧。

transcript.en: I need to go over this report one last time to make sure there are no mistakes.
transcript.zh: 我需要最后再看一遍这份报告，确保没有错误。

transcript.en: Can you help me go over my presentation?
transcript.zh: 你能帮我过一遍我的演示文稿吗？

transcript.en: I want to make sure it's perfect.
Let's go over these numbers one more time and make sure there are no mistakes.
transcript.zh: 我们再过一遍这些数字，确保没有错误。

transcript.en: Yeah, this is a really common word and it basically means look at carefully.
transcript.zh: 是的，这是一个非常常用的词，基本上意思是仔细查看。

transcript.en: In English, we often find simple little words, they fit together really well.
transcript.zh: 在英语中，我们经常发现一些简单的小词，它们组合得非常好。

transcript.en: And you think, oh, they're so easy, like the word go over, so easy.
transcript.zh: 你会觉得，哦，它们太简单了，比如 go over 这个词，太容易了。

transcript.en: But it's the way that they interact with each other that makes them...
transcript.zh: 但正是它们相互作用的方式让它们……

transcript.en: Or it makes you sound much better.
transcript.zh: 或者说让你的英语听起来好得多。

transcript.en: So go over, in this case, we might say, let's go over the lesson.
transcript.zh: 所以 go over，在这个情境中，我们可以说：让我们来过一遍这节课。
让我们来复习一下这节课。

transcript.en: Yeah, and that's a more natural way of saying something like that.
transcript.zh: 是的，这是一种更自然的表达方式。

transcript.en: Okay, so we've taken a look at our language takeaways for today.
transcript.zh: 好的，我们已经看完了今天的语言要点。

transcript.en: I think it's time to listen to the dialogue one more time.
transcript.zh: 我想是时候再听一遍对话了。

transcript.en: And this time, the dialogue will be slower so we can understand and listen to all the words we just talked about.
transcript.zh: 这次对话会慢一些，这样我们就能听懂并听到我们刚讨论过的所有词汇。

transcript.en: Okay, so now the last point on our agenda.
transcript.zh: 好的，现在是我们议程的最后一点。

transcript.en: Jill, let's go over the profit and loss statement.
transcript.zh: 吉尔，我们来过一遍损益表。

transcript.en: Well, the main issue here, as you can see, is that our expenses are through the roof.
transcript.zh: 嗯，如你所见，主要问题是我们的开支飞涨。

transcript.en: These numbers are off the charts.
Well, um, sir, the company expenditures on entertainment and travel are out of control.
transcript.zh: 嗯，先生，公司在娱乐和差旅方面的支出失控了。

transcript.en: Look at these bills, for example.
Just this month, we've paid over $20,000 for hotel charges.
transcript.zh: 仅这个月，我们就支付了超过两万美元的酒店费用。

transcript.en: The list goes on and on.
Here, this is a bill for $5,000 for spa treatments.
transcript.zh: 这里，这是一张五千美元的水疗账单。

transcript.en: $5,000 were expensed in one night at a place called Wild Things?
transcript.zh: 在一个叫 Wild Things 的地方一晚就花了五千美元？

transcript.en: Thank you for your very thorough analysis.
transcript.zh: 感谢你非常详尽的分析。

transcript.en: Yeah, and you know, I heard a lot of really great phrases in this dialogue that I'd like to look at now in Fluency Builder.
transcript.zh: 是的，你知道吗，我在这段对话中听到了很多非常棒的短语，现在我想在流利表达中看看。

transcript.en: So today on Fluency Builder, we have three words for you.
transcript.zh: 今天的流利表达，我们为大家准备了三个词。

transcript.en: Let's start by looking at the first one, off the charts.
transcript.zh: 让我们从第一个开始——off the charts（爆表/高得离谱）。

transcript.en: So this word is very similar to through the roof.
transcript.zh: 这个词和 through the roof 非常相似。

transcript.en: So let's listen to some examples of how we can use off the charts in a different situation.
transcript.zh: 让我们听几个在不同情境中使用 off the charts 的例子。

transcript.en: Oil prices have gone up and our costs are off the charts.
transcript.zh: 油价上涨了，我们的成本高得离谱。

transcript.en: Your sales are off the charts this year.
transcript.zh: 你今年的销售额爆表了。

transcript.en: Our losses are off the charts.
So Marco, do you think I can change off the charts for through the roof in these examples?
transcript.zh: 马可，你觉得这些例子中可以用 through the roof 替换 off the charts 吗？

transcript.en: You can use off the charts or through the roof.
transcript.zh: 你可以用 off the charts 或者 through the roof。

transcript.en: Both of them mean the same thing.
So two ways of saying really, really, really high.
transcript.zh: 所以是两种说「非常非常高」的方式。

transcript.en: But they're very commonly used in a business setting.
transcript.zh: 但它们在商务场合非常常用。

transcript.en: So this next word is a phrase that you can use if you want to tell somebody that you'll check something or you'll investigate something.
transcript.zh: 下一个词是一个短语，当你想要告诉某人你会查看或调查某事时可以用到。

transcript.en: And we heard it in our dialogue.
transcript.zh: 我们在对话中听到了它。

transcript.en: So let's listen to the clip.

transcript.zh: I'll look into it（我会调查一下）。
所以 look into that——去调查一下。
意思是我会去查一下某事。
是的，我去看看怎么回事。

transcript.en: Does it mean you're going to take action?
transcript.zh: 这意味着你会采取行动吗？

transcript.en: So I think we've got another word that does mean you're going to take action.
transcript.zh: 我想我们有另一个词确实意味着你会采取行动。
I'll take care of it（我会处理好的）。

transcript.en: So this word means that you're going to do something about it.
transcript.zh: 所以这个词的意思是你将对此做点什么。

transcript.en: So I will do something about it.
transcript.zh: 所以我会对此采取行动。

transcript.en: I will investigate and I'll do it.

transcript.zh: 再说一次，两个很棒的短语。

transcript.en: So now let's listen to the dialogue a third time.
transcript.zh: 现在让我们听第三遍对话。

transcript.en: It's going to be at its normal speed, but now you have all the tools you need to understand it a lot better.
transcript.zh: 这次是正常语速，但现在你已经掌握了所有需要的工具，可以理解得好得多。

transcript.en: So now the last point on our agenda.
transcript.zh: 好的，现在是我们议程的最后一点。

transcript.en: Jill, let's go over the profit and loss statement.
transcript.zh: 吉尔，我们来过一遍损益表。

transcript.en: Well, the main issue here, as you can see, is that our expenses are through the roof.
transcript.zh: 嗯，如你所见，主要问题是我们的开支飞涨。

transcript.en: These numbers are off the charts.
Well, sir, the company expenditures on entertainment and travel are out of control.
transcript.zh: 嗯，先生，公司在娱乐和差旅方面的支出失控了。

transcript.en: Look at these bills, for example.
Just this month, we've paid over $20,000 for hotel charges.
transcript.zh: 仅这个月，我们就支付了超过两万美元的酒店费用。

transcript.en: The list goes on and on.
Here, this is a bill for $5,000 for spa treatment.
transcript.zh: 这里，这是一张五千美元的水疗账单。

transcript.en: $8,000 were expensed in one night at a place called Wild Things.
transcript.zh: 在一个叫 Wild Things 的地方一晚就花了八千美元？

transcript.en: I'll do a very thorough analysis.
transcript.zh: 我会做一个非常详尽的分析。

transcript.en: Marco, I guess one of the benefits of being an executive in a company, especially a large company, is you get a lot of amazing benefits.
transcript.zh: 马可，我想在一家公司做高管的好处之一，尤其是一家大公司，就是你能得到很多很棒的福利。

transcript.en: When you are a manager or a CEO of one of these big companies, you get a lot of great things like, I don't know, a private jet maybe.
transcript.zh: 当你是这些大公司的经理或CEO时，你会得到很多好东西，比如，我不知道，也许私人飞机？

transcript.en: Or the company often pays for your house.
transcript.zh: 或者公司常常帮你付房费。

transcript.en: Or for your car, they'll give you a company car.
transcript.zh: 或者公司给你配一辆车。

transcript.en: They'll pay for your kids' or your children's tuition for high school.
transcript.zh: 他们会帮你付孩子的高中学费。

transcript.en: Also, I've heard about entertainment bonuses.
So you can go out to a restaurant, get the receipt, and claim the expenses at work.
transcript.zh: 所以你可以去餐厅吃饭，拿收据，然后在公司报销。

transcript.en: Those are some great benefits, right?
transcript.zh: 这些是很棒的福利，对吧？

transcript.en: So Marco, I'm curious to know what our listeners' expenses are.
transcript.zh: 马可，我很好奇我们听众的开支是什么。

transcript.en: We definitely want to know what crazy expenses you have.
transcript.zh: 我们绝对想知道你们有什么疯狂的开支。

transcript.en: My spending on Coke Zero has gone through the roof since we started this podcast.
transcript.zh: 自从我们开始这个播客以来，我在零度可乐上的花费就飞涨了。

transcript.en: You spend a lot of money on Coke Zeros every week, right?
transcript.zh: 你每周在零度可乐上花很多钱，对吧？

transcript.en: I probably have about, I don't know, 10 a week.
transcript.zh: 我大概一周喝，不知道，十罐吧。

transcript.en: Well, for example, I spend a lot on DVDs each week.
transcript.zh: 嗯，比如说，我每周在DVD上花很多钱。

transcript.en: I usually buy two or three movies.
That is off the charts for DVD spending.
transcript.zh: 在DVD消费上确实高得离谱。

transcript.en: So we want to know what you spend your money on.
transcript.zh: 所以我们想知道你把钱花在什么地方。

transcript.en: Be sure to go into our community website and tell us what you spend money on.
transcript.zh: 一定要去我们的社区网站，告诉我们你把钱花在哪里。

transcript.en: You can find us at EnglishPod.com.
transcript.zh: 你可以在 EnglishPod.com 找到我们。

transcript.en: And Marco and I are always there to respond to your questions and comments.
transcript.zh: 马可和我总是在那里回复你们的问题和评论。
